title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, free on the loops l_0 and l_1. ρ is the order-3 automorphism cyclically permuting the three punctures, with l_1 = ρ(l_0). σ_∞ (also written τ_∞) is the order-2 symmetry fixing ∞. The tilde-group Π̂_{0,3}·{1,τ_∞} is Π̂_{0,3} extended by this involution; here τ_∞ acts like complex conjugation, sending l_0 to l_0^{-1}.

The problem being solved (previous page). Grothendieck classifies the 'à lacets' (inertia-preserving) automorphisms u of Π̂_{0,3} that commute with ρ. Such a u sends l_0 to a conjugate of l_0^μ, with μ = 2ν+1 a unit of Ẑ. In the case g=1 he writes
- u(l_0) = int(f^{-1})(l_0^μ),
- u(σ_∞) = hσ_∞, where h must solve 'the equation in h': h σ_∞(h) = 1.
It was shown that h = f^{-1} l_0^ν (σ_∞ρ)(f). He then puts ψ = f ρ(f)^{-1} and η = l_0^{-ν} ψ. The equation in h becomes η σ_∞(η) = 1.

This page. It collects the system (24):
- ψ ρ(ψ) ρ²(ψ) = 1, a 3-cycle (ρ-cocycle) relation;
- η τ_∞(η) = 1, a 2-cycle relation;
- the compatibility ψ = l_0^ν η, which reduces to ψ = η when μ = 1.
These are structurally the hexagon/pentagon-free part of Drinfeld's GT relations: the 2-cycle f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 and the 3-cycle relation with exponent m, λ = 2m+1. Here μ = 2ν+1 plays the role of λ.

The extra condition. Grothendieck notes these relations are not sufficient. ψ must be 'principal': when the ρ-cocycle ψ is written as a coboundary ψ = f ρ(f)^{-1}, the element f must lie in Π̂_{0,3}, not merely in the extension by τ_∞. Equivalently, the image of f in the tilde-group modulo Π̂_{0,3}, which is Z/2, must vanish. One then recovers h from (21), and hence u.

Remark 1. If ψ is not principal, (21) still defines h with h τ_∞(h) = 1, hence an automorphism commuting with ρ. Writing f = τ_∞ f_0 gives u(l_0) = int(f_0^{-1})(l_0^{-μ}). So u is again 'à lacets', but with multiplier -μ (made explicit on the next page). The Z/2 ambiguity thus corresponds to the sign of the local multiplier.

Implicit reading. This is non-abelian H^1(Z/3, Π̂_{0,3}). A cocycle ψ gives an element ψρ of order 3 in Π̂ ⋊ Z/3, which is the profinite orbifold group of the Z/3-quotient. That quotient has two cone points of order 3 (the fixed points e^{±iπ/3}) and one puncture, so the group is Ẑ/3 * Ẑ/3 profinitely. Conjugacy classes of order-3 lifts of ρ correspond to the two cone points. The involution τ_∞ swaps them, which explains why every cocycle becomes a coboundary after allowing f in the τ_∞-extension, with a Z/2 obstruction.
errors: Notation drift: σ_∞ and τ_∞ are used interchangeably for the same involution, and h τ_∞(h)=1 is written for the equation previously written h σ_∞(h)=1.

The page silently assumes every ρ-cocycle ψ is a coboundary over the τ_∞-extension Π̂_{0,3}·{1,τ_∞}. This is true, via the profinite conjugacy theorem for torsion in free products of finite groups, but is not justified here.
In Remark 1, int(f^{-1}) with f = τ_∞ f_0 should involve int(f_0^{-1})∘int(τ_∞)^{±1}; the bookkeeping of order is slightly loose but the conclusion (multiplier -μ) is correct.

ideas.what: Reduction of ρ-commuting inertia-preserving automorphisms of Π̂_{0,3} to pairs (ψ,η) satisfying a 3-cycle and a 2-cycle relation with compatibility ψ = l_0^ν η, μ = 2ν+1
ideas.modern_name: 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations defining (part of) the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches GT-type ideas (Teichmüller tower, 'jeu de Lego'); these explicit relations are not there

ideas.what: Parametrization ψ = f ρ(f)^{-1} of ρ-cocycles, and a Z/2 obstruction ('principal' solutions) given by whether f lies in Π̂_{0,3} or only in its τ_∞-extension
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian H^1(Z/3, Π̂_{0,3}) and conjugacy of order-3 elements in the profinite orbifold group Ẑ/3 * Ẑ/3
ideas.usually_credited_to: Herfort–Ribes and others for profinite torsion conjugacy; unsure for this specific use in GT

ideas.what: Non-principal solutions yield inertia-preserving automorphisms with multiplier -μ

missed.claim: The extra 'principality' condition is identified with a Z/2-valued invariant: which of the two order-3 cone points of the Z/3-quotient orbifold the cocycle ψρ belongs to. This places the defining relations of a GT-like group within non-abelian Galois cohomology of the S_3-symmetry. It also explains the 3-cycle relation as a coboundary condition rather than an arbitrary equation.
missed.quote: il faut supposer que la solution ψ de l'équation (24) "en ψ" soit "principale", i.e. que, quand on écrit ψ sous forme paramétrique ψ = fρ(f)^{-1} avec f ∈ Π̂_{0,3}·{1,τ_∞}, on ait bien f ∈ Π̂_{0,3}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Standard GT literature imposes the 3-cycle relation directly. Grothendieck's coboundary parametrization (f ↦ ψ) and its Z/2 obstruction is a cohomological perspective on GT relations that is not standard. It also shows he had the GT 2- and 3-cycle relations, with exponent μ = 2ν+1, independently of and before Drinfeld.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Grothendieck deriving, in unpublished notes, essentially the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of GT, with the λ = 2m+1 exponent structure, plus an extra cohomological 'principal solution' Z/2 condition. Historians partly know he anticipated GT. The specific coboundary parametrization and Z/2 obstruction is a notable unpublished detail, but it is close to known theory.
transcription_corrections: The 'γ' before (24) is likely a margin mark; the label is just (24).
'en tous cas elle signifie ψ=η !' should read 'en ce cas elle signifie ψ=η !' (the case μ=1, ν=0).

'il faut supposer que les solutions [?] de l'équation (24) "en ψ" sont des solutions [?] : les fonctions principales' is more likely 'il faut supposer que la solution ψ de l'équation (24) "en ψ" soit "principale", i.e. que, quand on écrit ψ sous forme paramétrique'.
'on détermine u par (21), d'où u ... = 2' is more plausibly 'on détermine h par (21), d'où u' (with a crossed-out fragment).
The marginal note reads roughly 'On trouvera ensuite [?] soit ψ quoi [?]'; it is uncertain.
